text:
anna: quick follow-up to the onprem packaging rfc: i prototyped a tiny "delta entropy" smoke check for bundles operators can run pre-activation in air-gapped sites. aim: catch content surprises without heavyweight evals.

mike: curious how this works fully offline. air-gapped customers won't run model eval suites.

anna: two variants: (A) bundle includes an optional compact summary (token-frequency sketch, small ngram sample, optional embedding centroid); (B) operator computes a summary locally from the stored artifacts using a streaming tokenizer sample. comparisons are lightweight JS/KL-ish metrics on sketches.

sasha: operator surface: should this be part of the k8s operator or a separate sidecar? what actions on anomalies?

anna: prefer it baked into operator for lifecycle control. possible actions: block activation (fail), quarantine bundle, reduce canary fraction to zero, or proceed into phased activation requiring manual approval. operator emits a signed audit marker to the local sealed store when an approval occurs.

devon: sampling/compute limits are concerning for huge model files.

mike: keep default summaries tiny: 1% reservoir tokenizer sample or N tokens capped at 100k, plus a 256-bin token sketch (count-min like). sampling is streaming so memory bounded.

anna: heuristics i suggest: JS divergence on token-frequency sketch; top-k token mass delta; optional centroid cosine if embeddings included; coarse file-level jumps (size, new bin types). example thresholds: JS > 0.12 => soft-fail; centroid-dist > 0.08 => soft-fail. tunable per-customer.

sasha: privacy: can manifest summaries leak PII or proprietary traces?

anna: manifest must not include raw tokens. store sketches/sketch-hashes only, and require server-side signing of the summary. add privacy guidelines in RFC: no raw prompt snippets, no unredacted example inputs in summaries.

devon: upgrade UX: if operator approves a soft-fail, how do we avoid re-blocking on future installs?

mike: operator writes a signed activation marker into the sealed store: {bundle_id, summary_hash, approver, rationale, ts}. subsequent installs consult marker and skip the same soft-block if marker matches. markers are KMS-wrapped.

anna: pseudo manifest snippet i mocked:

```
manifest: {
  bundle_id: "delta-2026-09-01",
  artifacts: [...],
  entropy_summary: {
    token_sketch_b64: "<base64>",
    centroid_hash_b64: "<hash>",
    sample_size: "100000"
  },
  summary_signature: "<sig>"
}
```

sasha: suggest an operator API endpoint: POST /operator/v1/approve-entropy {bundle_id, approver, rationale, marker_sig} so distros can use uniform tooling.

devon: remember some customers forbid any manifest extras. flow must support operator-only mode where the operator computes and stores summaries locally and compares them to the active summary. manifest optionality is required.

mike: rollout pattern recommendation: fractional activation (1% canary) -> monitor local metrics and quality -> 10% -> full. operator shim should support sticky fraction markers and predictable rollback semantics.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: entropy_summary present: true. js_divergence_est: 0.18 -> result: soft-fail. action: hold activation pending manual approval. :warning:

anna: action items: 1) add optional entropy_summary schema to bundle manifest RFC, 2) define operator shim API and activation marker format, 3) publish threshold defaults and telemetry events, 4) ship a small airgap-friendly sample generator (go/python) that creates sketches offline.

mike: i'll own item 2 and the approve API sketch.

sasha: i'll draft the manifest schema and the privacy guidelines.

devon: i'll prototype a streaming tokenizer sampler with constant memory.

anna: thanks — i'll incorporate these into the RFC follow-up and open a PR this week :thumbsup:
